newsitem.title: GERMANY: Three Germans killed in fire at Luebeck shelter.
newsitem.headline: Three Germans killed in fire at Luebeck shelter.

text.p: Three homeless people were killed in a fire that destroyed a shelter in the northern German city of Luebeck on Wednesday, police said.
Authorities said they did not know what caused the blaze, which spread rapidly through the wooden building. They were investigating the possiblity of arson, one official said.
About 20 people lived in the shelter in the northern St Lorenz section of Luebeck.
The fire occurred just days after another blaze in Luebeck on Sunday started by suspected neo-Nazis destroyed a Roman Catholic church.

The arsonists daubed swastikas on the facade of St Vicelin Church and set a fire which spread. They also scrawled the name of a local priest whose parish is sheltering a family of asylum seekers to prevent their deportation back to Algeria.
The attack sparked memories of a wave of racist violence after German unification in 1990 in which asylum-seekers' hostels became frequent targets of firebombings.
